comparisons.peer_summary: Consumer IoT products are adopting latest mobile connectivity and on-device AI capabilities, with new AI-focused PCs launching in 2024 and analysts expecting 50% of PCs sold to be AI capable by 2027.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and QCOM identify on-device AI capabilities as a primary demand driver for memory and storage in mobile and personal computing devices. MU states that 'Enabling these on-device AI capabilities is driving increased memory and storage capacity needs,' while QCOM notes that consumer IoT and AI PCs are adopting 'on-device AI capabilities' which drive new services and experiences. QCOM provides a specific forecast for AI-capable PCs (50% by 2027), whereas MU focuses on the resulting hardware requirement for 'high-performance memory' and 'storage capacity'.

sentences.text: Smartphones offer tremendous potential for personalized AI capabilities that offer greater security and responsiveness when executed on the device.
Enabling these on-device AI capabilities is driving increased memory and storage capacity needs and increasing demand for new value-add solutions.

Consumer IoT products, including personal computing (e.g., tablets and PCs), voice and music and XR, continue to adopt the latest mobile connectivity, processing and intelligence technologies including on-device AI capabilities.
This enables new services, applications and experiences that can be run directly on the device, driving improvements in latency, cost and privacy.

comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm expects continued advancement in edge device generative AI capabilities, with analysts estimating 46% of smartphones sold in 2027 will be generative AI capable, up from 19% in 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures address the growth of AI capabilities in mobile handsets. MU attributes the need for increased memory and storage in smartphones to 'on-device AI capabilities,' while QCOM explicitly forecasts that '46% of smartphones sold in 2027 will be generative AI capable,' reflecting the same underlying market trend driving MU's memory demand thesis.

sentences.text: Enabling these on-device AI capabilities is driving increased memory and storage capacity needs and increasing demand for new value-add solutions.
We expect continued advancement in the generative AI capabilities of edge devices and increased adoption of generative AI capable technologies in handsets and other edge devices.
For example, analysts estimate that 46% of smartphones sold in 2027 will be generative AI capable, up from 19% in 2024 (Counterpoint, October 2024).
